$comment: The curated layer of the project's language corpus. scripts/corpus.mjs
harvests the site's own en/zh pairs first — those are the authority for
anything a buyer reads — and merges this file on top of them.
So this file holds ONLY what the site never says: the report's design,
commerce and legal vocabulary, the terms that must stay in Latin script,
the dual renderings the project has looked at and settled, and the words
Adding a term here makes it enforced: scripts/check-corpus.mjs reports a
translated passage that contains the English and not this Chinese.
Nothing already in site.json, seller.json, artworks.json or build.js
belongs here — it would be a second copy of a string that already has an
owner, and the two would drift.
$termsNote: Short entries are enforced terms; a long one is offered as memory only.
`note` records why a choice was made where it was not obvious — the same
standard the rest of this repository is commented to.

terms.note: A gate that refuses, not a checklist that reminds. 闸门 keeps the refusal.
Throughout the report a ground is the surface text is set on, never soil.
The pale card a painting is mounted on, not a printing plate.
The empty box a missing glyph draws. 豆腐块 is what Chinese typographers call it.
A facet across series, so 题材 rather than 类型.

terms.zh: 市场监管总局第 37 号令

terms.note: Matches build.js's returns page, which is where a buyer meets the word.

terms.$note: Promoted from site labels. Both are single words harvested from site.json, so the corpus offers them but does not enforce them until they are named here — and in prose these two do mean one thing each.

terms.note: The series title. A painting in it is 《致敬》系列, not a tribute in the ordinary sense.

$keepNote: Latin script, verbatim, in Chinese prose. Three reasons appear here:
a product with no Chinese name (Stripe, Airwallex, tectonic); a standard
cited by its Latin designation (WCAG, RFC 2606); and a person, typeface
or term of art that is read in Latin by the people who use it (Fraunces,
sfumato). Anything inside backticks in the report is protected already —
file names, CSS variables and hex values never reach this list.
$splitsNote: One English term, two Chinese renderings, on purpose. Each is a case the
project has looked at and settled; scripts/check-corpus.mjs reports any
split that is NOT listed here, which is how an accidental one is caught.

splits.why: 作品 is the heading and the thing; 件作品 is the counter, as in 6 件作品. A Chinese counter cannot be dropped, and a heading cannot carry one.

$furnitureNote: The words of the document's own furniture — title page, running heads,
part label, index, float captions. preamble.tex routes every one of these
through a macro with the English as its default; translate.mjs writes the
Chinese ones out as report-zh-strings.tex, so there is no second copy of
them kept by hand in a .tex file.

blurb.en: Unique paintings, sold from mainland China to buyers at home and abroad. What follows is what that costs, what it requires, and what is still unresolved.
blurb.zh: 独一无二的画作，自中国大陆售往国内与海外的买家。以下写明这件事的成本、前提，以及尚未解决的部分。

partAfter.note: Chinese counts a part as 第 N 部分, so the label wraps the number instead of preceding it. The English default is empty.
